subtitle: Get to know the five orientations of the Intercultural Development Continuum (IDC) and use the model to ask better learning questions, without using it to label people.
scope: For staff across DHS. This conceptual introduction does not administer, reproduce or score the IDI and cannot determine a person’s or team’s orientation. Practice statements illustrate ideas, not diagnoses. Actual IDI participation and results belong to their authorized assessment and development process. Work decisions, records and formal concerns retain their appropriate routes. Matters involving Native American communities or Tribal relations should be referred to the appropriate office within ADSA. Optional reflection may be entirely private or unrecorded, with the practice case available; personal growth does not require measurable work proof.
introTranscript: The Intercultural Development Continuum, or IDC, offers five orientations toward cultural difference and similarity. This course uses the meanings described in the examples of welcome, belonging and privacy to explore the questions those concepts raise. Personal reflection may remain private and is valuable without a work product; suitable workplace application is another path. These examples do not assess a person or rank staff. In this program, Integration means the people a process affects help design it; it does not add a sixth official IDC orientation.

intro.heading: Read the continuum as a learning model
intro.body:
The official sequence is Denial, Polarization, Minimization, Acceptance and Adaptation. The names refer to orientations in a developmental model. They are not job titles, employee grades or a shortcut for judging the quality of a colleague from one exchange. A course can explain the concepts and provide practice without assessing the learner.

In a practice DHS review, a facilitator brings several sample statements about how the team handles disagreement. Participants can examine what a statement overlooks or assumes. They cannot use a sentence from a real colleague to place that colleague on the continuum. The same work response can have several explanations, and an appropriate assessment has its own process.

Keep a model question separate from the actual work decision. A team still needs evidence, required review and clear responsibility for the proposal it is considering. Naming a concept does not decide whether the proposal is sound, whether conduct violates policy or who has authority. The model can inform reflection while those questions use their proper routes.

The program also uses the word Integration. In this program, Integration means the people a process affects help design it; the name comes from Bennett’s developmental model, where it describes identity across cultures. It does not add Integration as a sixth orientation to the official IDC. Likewise, Foundations, applied and more complex course levels describe the scope of learning activities rather than a person’s presumed IDC placement.

flashcards.back: The Intercultural Development Continuum: a developmental model with five official orientations toward cultural difference and similarity.
An orientation in the model that gives limited attention to relevant cultural difference.
An orientation in the model that judges difference through opposing group evaluations.
An orientation in the model that emphasizes commonality in ways that can obscure relevant difference.
An orientation in the model that recognizes and seeks to understand cultural difference and commonality.
The official IDC orientation involving culturally informed perspective shifting and an appropriate change in behavior across difference; this course does not assign it to a person.
In this program, the people a process affects help design it; not a sixth official IDC orientation or a personal assessment result.

items.title: Keep the names accurate
items.body: The facilitator writes the five official names in their sequence and identifies them as model concepts. Adding another orientation would blur the distinction between this framework and program application. Staff can still discuss how learning becomes part of ordinary work, but should name that as application rather than alter the official sequence.

items.title: A statement is limited evidence
items.body: A sentence can provide a useful prompt about a way of interpreting difference. It does not show the speaker’s complete perspective, context or assessment result. In practice, discuss what the actual proposal or response does and what needs checking instead of turning the model into a label for someone.

items.title: Learning levels serve a different purpose
items.body: A later course may involve a more complex policy or organizational task. That complexity does not establish that its participants are personally more important or occupy a particular orientation. Choose learning for the capability and work situation, keeping personal assessment separate and optional program practice understandable.

tabs.label: Model learning
tabs.body: The model can open a question about how you understand a culturally learned meaning. You might privately explore what welcome or privacy means to you, or use the practice examples. This personal insight has value without a work product. If a workplace effect is claimed, its actual evidence and responsibility remain separate.

tabs.label: Personal labeling
tabs.body: Personal labeling may look efficient but turns a fragment of behavior into an unsupported assessment. It can discourage feedback and make learning feel like a hierarchy. Explain the concept without deciding where a colleague belongs, and use the proper assessment process for actual results.

tabs.label: Personal or work application
tabs.body: Application may involve a more nuanced private understanding or a suitable response in an interaction. Neither adds an official orientation or establishes an assessment placement. Work decisions retain their actual requirements; a private reflection does not need to become a task record to count as learning.

check.feedbackIncorrect: Answers to course exercises do not administer the IDI. Program Integration is not a sixth official orientation. Course complexity does not rank people’s importance. intro.heading: Distinguish overlooking difference from judging difference
intro.body:
Denial and Polarization are different official IDC concepts. Denial involves limited recognition of cultural difference; Polarization uses opposing evaluations, including favoring a familiar group or reversing that judgment. The following practice statements illustrate questions about these ideas. They cannot establish the orientation of a speaker or learner.

Mara organizes an optional DHS welcome circle and invites everyone to share a meaningful personal story. Family and community experiences important to Mara taught that sharing stories is a warm expression of welcome. Dev declines. Dev voluntarily explains another learned meaning: being allowed time and choice before sharing personal experience communicates respect and makes connection feel trustworthy. These are individual invented accounts, not national, racial, faith or other group rules.

One sample statement says there are no different meanings here; a welcome is simply a welcome, so nothing needs exploring. It leaves the learned meanings of sharing and privacy unexamined. A second says our people are warm and their people are cold. That statement ranks presumed groups rather than considering Dev’s account. Reversing the claim so one supposed group is automatically superior would still replace inquiry with opposing evaluations.

Mara can ask what the invitation means in the two accounts and whether a choice would communicate welcome more appropriately. Dev need not provide further personal history. No one should be labeled Denial or Polarization from declining an activity or using a sample sentence. Operational circumstances and individual preference can also matter; avoid declaring culture the cause of every response.

The optional activity remains separate from actual onboarding duties and required work information. Understanding its relational meaning does not waive a required orientation step or authorize recording private stories. You may explore your own meaning privately or use Mara and Dev without entering a personal account.

items.title: An unseen cultural meaning
items.body: The no-difference statement treats Mara’s learned expression of welcome as self-evident. Dev’s account reveals a different possible meaning: choice and time can convey respect. Examine that meaning rather than making a personal orientation claim from a refusal to share.

items.title: An opposing-group judgment
items.body: Warm people versus cold people assigns worth to presumed groups instead of listening to the individual account. It can turn a voluntary boundary into a character defect. Idealizing the other group automatically would also miss the actual meanings and context.

items.title: A relevant next inquiry
items.body: Ask what sharing or allowing choice means to each person. Mara may privately explore the familiar value of storytelling while considering another expression of welcome. No further disclosure, group representation or workplace metric is required for that personal understanding.

tabs.label: Treat meaning as absent
tabs.body: Treating the invitation as culturally neutral may hide a learned expectation about closeness and sharing. The activity could feel warm to one person and pressured to another. The inquiry should examine expressed meaning, not assert that every refusal has a cultural cause.

tabs.label: Rank presumed groups
tabs.body: A warm-versus-cold ranking supplies an unsupported group evaluation. It does not tell Mara how Dev understands welcome, and it can make privacy seem disloyal. Use the individual account rather than a superiority or inferiority story.

tabs.label: Explore meanings
tabs.body: Mara can examine the familiar story-sharing meaning alongside Dev’s volunteered meaning of chosen connection. This opens a more accurate question without devaluing either person or diagnosing them. Actual work requirements remain separate from the optional welcome activity.

check.question: Which comparison accurately describes the practice statements?
check.correct: The no-difference statement leaves learned meanings unseen; the warm-versus-cold statement ranks presumed groups instead of examining Dev’s account.
wrong: Dev’s refusal proves Dev’s official IDI placement.
A warm-versus-cold ranking is enough to determine everyone’s value.
Every declined activity must be caused by cultural identity.
check.feedbackCorrect: The comparison concerns the statements and meanings while preserving individual variation and assessment limits.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Declining an optional activity does not determine an IDI result. A group ranking does not establish personal value or meaning. Refusal may have many causes, so identity is not the automatic explanation. Examine the expressed account and the question each practice statement closes.

intro.heading: Examine common ground without flattening difference
intro.body:
Minimization emphasizes commonality in ways that can obscure relevant cultural difference. Shared humanity and common goals can support connection; the problem is using them to stop exploring culturally learned meanings. A common wish does not establish that everyone experiences the same expression in the same way.

In the practice welcome circle, Mara says we all want to belong, so everyone should share a personal story in the same public way. Wanting belonging is a useful common starting point. It does not settle the learned meanings of closeness, privacy and respect. In Dev’s voluntary account, choice and time support trustworthy connection; compelled immediate sharing could communicate disregard.

Mara can retain the wish to welcome colleagues and examine what the activity assumes. A participant may choose to listen, offer a nonsensitive practice example or join a suitable later conversation where appropriate. These are illustrative options for an optional activity, not a new agency procedure or a rule about every group. The actual context, resources and duties still matter.

The model concept should not be assigned to Mara from one statement. Nor does equal respect require approving any requested action or ignoring actual conduct concerns. This exercise examines how commonality can conceal meaning. It does not determine formal policy outcomes or abolish shared expectations.

You may privately ask whether a familiar way of belonging felt universal to you and what another expressed meaning reveals. That insight is valuable without a work result or public story. The practice case provides an alternative to personal reflection.

items.title: Common ground remains valuable
items.body: Mara and Dev can both value connection without expressing it identically. The shared wish can support further inquiry. Rejecting all commonality would miss this resource; treating it as a complete explanation would hide the different meanings of sharing and choice.

items.title: A familiar expression can obscure meaning
items.body: The same public story request may communicate warmth in Mara’s account and pressure in Dev’s. This is not a claim about all people with similar backgrounds. Examine the volunteered meaning and allow choice rather than predicting a group preference.

items.title: A suitable optional arrangement
items.body: Listening or using an example may allow participation in the optional circle without personal disclosure. The required work introduction remains separate. Do not promise a change to actual onboarding duties merely to demonstrate flexibility in this learning case.

tabs.label: Commonality ends inquiry
tabs.body: We all want belonging can become reassurance that the familiar activity must fit everyone. Dev’s account shows why the shared wish leaves an expression question open. Retain the common wish and explore meaning rather than turning difference into reluctance to belong.

tabs.label: Every difference removes standards
tabs.body: Noticing difference does not authorize unsafe conduct, a required-duty waiver or every proposed method. The case concerns an optional sharing activity. Keep actual responsibilities and protections while considering a suitable response to the individual account.

tabs.label: Common purpose and meaning
tabs.body: A combined response retains welcome and asks how choice or time may communicate it. Mara need not reject storytelling, and Dev need not adopt it as the only expression. Understanding the distinction supports personal growth and an optional appropriate activity change.

check.feedbackCorrect: The answer retains common ground while examining the culturally learned expression it does not settle.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A shared wish does not prove identical public sharing is suitable. Noticing difference does not waive duties. One statement cannot administer the IDI. Examine the expressed meanings and context rather than using commonality as a shortcut or making it inherently harmful.

intro.heading: Understand a perspective without treating it as approval
intro.body:
Acceptance in the official IDC involves recognizing and appreciating cultural differences and commonalities, including contrasting reflection on one’s own cultural pattern. This course asks what you can understand through comparison; it does not label a person Acceptance or equate understanding with agreeing to every action.

Mara learned to associate a shared story with warm welcome. Dev’s volunteered account associates chosen time and privacy with respectful connection. Mara can see how both expressions make sense from the experiences described. The change is more than learning a preference: Mara begins examining how a familiar meaning became the assumed standard for everyone.

This understanding can be a worthwhile personal result. A learner may privately notice a valued expression of welcome and recognize another possible expression without rejecting the original. Explore the example at your own pace. You can keep your reflections private. The practice comparison is equally available.

In optional work application, Mara still considers what is appropriate in the actual setting. A revised voluntary activity should not pressure Dev to explain more or alter formal onboarding requirements outside authority. Understanding why choice matters does not itself decide every proposed method, resource or policy question.

Acceptance in the model is not automatically the ability to make every response suitable. Further inquiry and practice may be needed. Recognize what the account clarified, what remains unknown and which actual decision or duty is separate. This keeps appreciation of meaning distinct from a certificate of correctness or permission to ignore harm.

items.title: Meaning without automatic approval
items.body: Mara can understand why chosen time communicates respect in Dev’s account without promising every possible activity change. The account deserves attention, while actual conduct, resources and formal responsibilities retain their own processes. Understanding is not a universal waiver.

items.title: Comparison includes yourself
items.body: Mara asks how storytelling became a familiar expression of warmth and compares that meaning with chosen privacy. The original value need not be discarded. Privately making the familiar assumption visible can be a meaningful personal insight rather than an obligatory work plan.

items.title: Understanding leaves questions open
items.body: A suitable voluntary alternative may need practical consideration. Acceptance of another meaning does not guarantee that Mara can respond appropriately in every setting. Keep the learned insight and ask what a context-sensitive next response would need.

tabs.label: Automatic endorsement
tabs.body: Treating understanding as approval of every proposed action conflates meaning with authority. Choice may be relevant to the optional circle, but the account cannot waive mandatory onboarding or other formal duties. Acknowledge meaning and examine the actual action separately.

tabs.label: Dismiss the account
tabs.body: Dismissing Dev’s account preserves Mara’s familiar standard without examining its scope. Neither agreement nor a personal story is required to listen proportionately. Compare the meanings and permit the contributor to stop sharing rather than make proof of belonging depend on disclosure.

tabs.label: Understand and reflect
tabs.body: Mara can value storytelling and understand chosen privacy as another expression of respect. This personal perspective gain is legitimate even without a changed activity. If Mara proposes an optional response, its suitability and actual responsibilities should be examined separately.

intro.heading: Connect perspective with a suitable change in response
intro.body:
Adaptation in the official IDC concerns the ability to shift cultural perspective and behave appropriately across difference. The cognitive and behavioral parts belong together. An ordinary information fix or convenient scheduling change may be useful, but it does not alone explain the culturally informed connection.

Mara revises the familiar frame: declining a public personal story need not mean rejecting welcome; chosen time and privacy may express respectful connection in Dev’s account. Mara then makes personal sharing explicitly optional, welcomes listening or a nonsensitive practice contribution, and offers a suitable later interaction where appropriate. The response follows the expressed meaning rather than merely changing the order of an agenda.

The response can remain authentic. Mara may still value stories while recognizing another expression. Copying a presumed cultural manner or declaring that everyone associated with Dev prefers privacy would replace inquiry with performance or a group rule. The account is individual and contextual, and Dev can choose not to explain further.

Actual duties remain. The optional circle cannot waive a required orientation item or grant an invented right to change agency records. A proposed formal change follows its real authority. Interculturally informed response does not remove accountability or make every preference automatically appropriate.

This case illustrates meaning, perspective shift and behavior; it does not administer an assessment or establish Adaptation for Mara or the learner. Review the specific response and its limits, or privately consider how another meaning could inform a personal interaction without entering a record or proving a work result.

items.title: The frame shift is explicit
items.body: Mara moves from declining my familiar welcome means rejecting connection to chosen privacy may itself communicate respect. This shift uses Dev’s volunteered meaning. It is different from simply allowing a later agenda item because a room was unavailable.

items.title: Behavior follows the meaning
items.body: Making personal sharing optional and welcoming listening responds to the expressed need for chosen connection. Mara need not imitate Dev or reject storytelling. The response should suit the actual activity and remain open to correction rather than become a universal rule about identities.

items.title: Illustration is not assessment
items.body: One suitable exchange cannot establish a whole orientation or guarantee future behavior. The course illustrates the connection and keeps actual assessment separate. Formal duties and records remain governed by their own requirements, even when a voluntary activity is revised.

tabs.label: Different method only
tabs.body: A new agenda or a clearer instruction may improve coordination. To explain the culturally informed part, identify the learned meaning and how it changed the familiar frame and response. The new method alone cannot certify Adaptation or establish that the whole interaction fits.

tabs.label: Identity performance or waiver
tabs.body: A presumed group gesture, speech imitation or universal privacy rule ignores the individual account. Waiving an actual onboarding duty also exceeds the optional activity. Choose an authentic response tied to meaning and context, retaining the relevant boundaries.

tabs.label: Perspective and behavior
tabs.body: Mara understands chosen privacy as a possible expression of respectful connection and makes optional participation genuinely optional. This links meaning and response while retaining actual duties. It illustrates a capability without claiming an IDI result or universal group preference.

intro.heading: Use the model without making it a ranking tool
intro.body:
A useful model question can examine what cultural meaning you overlooked, what opposing evaluation you supplied, which commonality closed inquiry or how understood meaning could inform a response. These are course-proposed prompts, not scoring rules or proprietary assessment items. They cannot calculate a person’s orientation.

In the practice welcome case, Mara can privately reflect on why stories signaled warmth and what Dev’s meaning of chosen privacy reveals. That personal insight is worthwhile by itself. For optional work application, Mara can consider suitable participation choices and review whether the invitation honored their voluntary nature. A new actual policy or required orientation change would need its own process.

No learner must disclose a personal story or accept a homemade label before using resources. Private or unrecorded reflection and the practice alternative are available. Staff across DHS may use consultant guidance to develop their capability, while retaining their work and appropriate decision responsibilities.

Use the five official names accurately. Course levels describe learning scope; program Integration means the people a process affects help design it, not adding a sixth official orientation. Keep actual IDI results in their authorized process. Continue with another meaningful private question or suitable practice rather than turning the model into a hidden employee ranking.

lessons.keyStatement: Let the model sharpen inquiry and practice while keeping assessment separate.

items.title: A meaning question
items.body: What did I assume welcome must look like? opens Mara’s reflection. The question can lead to deeper personal understanding without an action record. Which colleague is less developed would instead demand an unsupported personal judgment. Use the practice meanings or your own private question.

items.title: No new participation gate
items.body: A program resource should not require a learner to accept a homemade cultural label before receiving guidance. Staff can work with practice examples or their own nonsensitive practice questions. The consultant supports capability through knowledge and feedback, while actual work responsibilities and formal routes remain available.

items.title: A bounded review
items.body: If Mara changes the optional invitation, its effect needs appropriate evidence and honest limits. The personal insight does not depend on that work outcome to matter. Neither a revised activity nor a course answer can establish an IDI result or prove every structural issue resolved.

tabs.label: Hidden employee ranking
tabs.body: Hidden ranking can turn reflective questions into an unofficial personnel measure. Answers to course exercises do not support that use. Discuss the behavior or work instruction and its evidence, keeping actual assessment and personnel processes separate rather than inferring a cultural score.

tabs.label: Personal inquiry and optional practice
tabs.body: Knowing the names can support a meaningful question about familiar and different cultural meanings. That question may remain private, with no required work product. An optional practice or suitable work response can deepen practice, while formal duties and assessment remain separate.

tabs.label: Inquiry with honest limits
tabs.body: Use the concept to open understanding, not rank a person. A private insight or practice meaning-to-response exercise can be valuable. If an operational effect is reported, keep its scope and actual responsibilities clear without making it the sole test of learning value.

wrong: Compute employees’ hidden orientation scores from their course answers.

check.feedbackCorrect: The use connects concepts to practical learning while preserving assessment, participation and official-model boundaries.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Course answers cannot compute IDI results or justify hidden employee rankings. A homemade label should not become a resource-access gate. Program Integration is not an official sixth orientation. Use the model to sharpen a reflective question and review a suitable practice with its actual evidence limits.
